body:
Create an emoji mnemonic for the fixed German lemma's meaning at <TARGET> in markedContext. The learner sees the lemma beside the emojis.

Determine what the marked expression means HERE, including figurative uses. Represent that meaning, not another sense of the same word, not the surrounding scene, and not a neighbouring word's meaning. A copula, light verb, or other verb whose sentence meaning is carried by its complement contributes only its own part (staying, becoming, causing, seeming). Leave the complement out entirely, even as a second emoji; its state belongs to its own lemma.

Choose one to four familiar emojis. Start from the single emoji that already carries the meaning; add another only when it removes a real ambiguity or supplies a missing part. Never append a negation or emphasis sign to an emoji that already expresses the state. Prefer recognizable symbols and expressive faces over clever rebuses. For an adjective, express the property or the feeling it causes. Preserve required effort versus possessed strength, upward versus downward movement, and positive versus negative feelings.

Describe the meaning so the mnemonic also works in other sentences with that meaning. Do not add incidental participants or objects from this sentence. Interpret idioms as a whole; compose transparent word parts only when helpful. Keep closely related meanings broad, but do not merge meanings whose combination would mislead a beginner.

Return only one to four emoji graphemes, directly as text.

input.markedContext: Wir sitzen auf einer <TARGET>Bank</TARGET> im Park.
Klicke mit der <TARGET>Maus</TARGET> auf das Symbol.
